context: Adding mechanical enforcement against agent slop in a TypeScript repo that already lints with Oxlint. The skill-specific part: offer vendoring the dmmulroy/anti-slop Oxlint rules (copied and owned, run by the installed toolchain), baseline existing violations before making new rules blocking, and keep policy in the existing linter and gate rather than a new linter or shell checks.

checklist.name: anti-slop rules vendored or offered
checklist.description: The solution vendors the dmmulroy/anti-slop Oxlint rules into the repository (rule source copied and owned, run by the installed oxlint) or explicitly offers doing so in enforcement-notes.md, rather than inventing custom slop detection from scratch without mentioning them

checklist.name: Baseline before blocking
checklist.description: Enabling the new rules does not break `npm run verify` on existing code: existing violations in src/ are fixed, recorded as a baseline, or the new rules start as warnings with a stated step to promote them to errors; enforcement-notes.md describes this rollout

checklist.name: Existing linter and gate own the policy
checklist.description: Enforcement lives in the Oxlint configuration reached by `npm run lint` / `npm run verify`; no second linter (ESLint, Biome) is introduced and no grep- or shell-based slop checks are added

checklist.name: Built-in rules cover what they can
checklist.description: Uses Oxlint's own rules where they exist, for example explicit-any and empty-block or empty-catch rules

checklist.name: Notes map rule to slop
checklist.description: enforcement-notes.md maps each named slop pattern (any casts, empty catch, narrating comments, barrel re-exports) to what catches it, and says plainly which ones remain review-only if none catches them
